row.title: Missing validation on parseInt for --max-turns option
row.detail: Line 190 calls `parseInt(opts.maxTurns)` without validation. If opts.maxTurns is invalid, parseInt returns NaN, which is passed upstream without validation.
row.fix: Add validation with Number.isNaN() before returning, or use a safer parsing function.
row.verify_note: Real bug that causes silent failure: the turn loop will not execute any turns when an invalid --max-turns value is provided. Default value works correctly. Severity is medium (not high) because it only occurs with explicit user error and gracefully degrades to no execution rather than crashing.
row.verify_reason: Line 190 in main.ts calls `parseInt(opts.maxTurns)` without validation. If opts.maxTurns is an invalid string (e.g., "--max-turns abc"), parseInt returns NaN. The NaN value is then passed downstream and reaches TurnLoopConfig.maxTurns at engine.ts:1354 as `this.config.maxTurns ?? 100`. However, the nullish coalescing operator (??) only checks for null/undefined, not NaN, so NaN is preserved. At turn-loop.ts:243, the loop condition `while (this.turnCount < this.config.maxTurns)` fails because any comparison with NaN returns false (e.g., `0 < NaN` is false), preventing any turns from executing. Verified with: `NaN ?? 100` returns NaN (not 100), and `0 < NaN` returns false.

row.title: Command injection vulnerability via unsanitized git diff argument
row.detail: The `_arg` parameter (user input) is interpolated directly into shell commands without escaping: `execSync(\`git diff --stat HEAD ${file}\`, ...)`. An attacker could pass shell metacharacters like `; rm -rf /` or backticks to execute arbitrary commands. This affects both the stat and diff commands at these lines.
row.fix: Use `execFileSync` instead of `execSync` to avoid shell interpretation, or properly escape the file argument using a library like `shell-escape` before interpolation.
row.verify_note: This is a clear command injection vulnerability affecting both lines 512 and 523 in the /diff command. The user input from the command dispatcher (registry.ts line 108) flows directly into shell command execution without any constraints or sanitization. The fix should use execFileSync instead of execSync, or properly escape file arguments using proper escaping mechanisms before interpolation.
row.verify_reason: The /diff command in core-commands.ts (lines 512 and 523) directly interpolates the user-provided `_arg` parameter into shell command templates without any sanitization or escaping. The code `execSync(\`git diff --stat HEAD ${file}\`, ...)` passes a backtick template literal to execSync, which interprets it as a shell command. This allows an attacker to inject shell metacharacters like `; rm -rf /` or backticks to execute arbitrary commands. Tested locally: passing `file.txt; touch /tmp/pwned.txt #` successfully creates /tmp/pwned.txt despite the git command failing, confirming command injection works.
